newsitem.title: USA: Lake vows to provide unvarnished intelligence.
newsitem.headline: Lake vows to provide unvarnished intelligence.

text.p: President Clinton's choice to head the troubled CIA vowed Tuesday to provide straight, unvarnished intelligence to decisionmakers and do even more than mandated by law to keep Congress informed if confirmed by the Senate.

At the start of twice-postponed, politically sensitive confirmation hearings, Anthony Lake said his previous job as Clinton's first-term national security adviser would in no way shade his thinking or analysis.

"Some have asked whether I -- as a close associate of President Clinton and participant in policy discussions -- can and will provide him the intelligence straight," he said in a prepared statement to the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence.
"This is indeed an appropriate question. The answer, unequivocably, is 'yes'," Lake went on. "I know first-hand how important it is to defend the bright line separating policy and intelligence."
Lake said he had no apologies for his decision to keep Congress in the dark about President Clinton's tacit approval of Iranian arms shipments to Bosnian Moslems in 1994.

"But I do appreciate that it would have been better to have informed key members of Congress on a discrete basis," he said, pledging to "go beyond" legal requirements to keep Congress informed of intelligence secrets.
